question: In Nigeria's health system, what is the main purpose of primary health care (PHC) facilities?

options.B: Serving as the first point of contact for communities

explanation: You've got this! PHC centers are set up right in the heart of our communities, making them the very first place people go when they need healthcare. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T1#BMP110_U2_T1_h1)

question: Which level of government in Nigeria is directly responsible for running federal teaching hospitals?
explanation: Teaching hospitals are major national institutions, so they are funded and managed directly by the federal government. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T1#BMP110_U2_T1_h1)

question: What is the main job of the Central Sterile Supply Department (CSSD) in a hospital?

options.A: Managing patient billing and financial records
options.B: Processing, sterilizing, and distributing medical equipment
options.C: Conducting laboratory tests on blood samples
options.D: Preparing specialized meals for admitted patients

explanation: Think of CSSD as the hospital's safety shield! They make sure all surgical tools and equipment are thoroughly cleaned, sterilized, and safe for patient use. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T1#BMP110_U2_T1_h2)

question: A woman is bleeding heavily after birth (postpartum hemorrhage). Which hospital unit should the midwife call most urgently for life-saving help?
explanation: In a severe bleeding emergency, every second counts. The blood bank and lab are vital for quickly testing blood and getting blood products ready to save her life. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T1#BMP110_U2_T1_h2)

question: Why must clean and dirty utility rooms always be kept separate on a hospital ward?

options.A: To minimize the risk of cross-infection
options.B: To comply with patient financial billing rules
options.C: To increase the storage space for medical books
options.D: To reduce the time spent writing reports

explanation: Keeping clean and dirty items apart is a golden rule of infection control. It stops germs from spreading and keeps our patients safe! [learn more](BMP110_U2_T1#BMP110_U2_T1_h3)

question: What is the most important thing a ward manager looks at when making a duty roster for nurses?

options.A: Ensuring every nurse works only night duties
options.B: Matching patient acuity and staff skill mix
options.C: Reducing the total number of working hours to zero
options.D: Giving preference to senior staff for weekend shifts

explanation: Great rostering is all about teamwork and patient needs—making sure we have the right mix of skilled hands on duty to care for how sick the patients are. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T1#BMP110_U2_T1_h3)

question: Who is mainly responsible for managing ward supplies and checking staff performance?
explanation: The Nursing Officer in Charge (NOIC) is the leader of the ward team, handling everything from daily supplies to staff evaluations. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T1#BMP110_U2_T1_h4)

question: As a student midwife on the postnatal ward, what is your correct and safe role?

options.B: Discharging patients without consulting qualified staff
options.C: Taking full administrative charge of the entire hospital
options.D: Performing clinical tasks under direct qualified supervision

explanation: You are learning! Always perform your clinical duties while being guided and supervised by your qualified mentors. You're never alone in this journey. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T1#BMP110_U2_T1_h4)

question: In the ISBAR handover tool, what does the letter 'S' stand for?
explanation: ISBAR helps us communicate clearly. The 'S' stands for Situation (what is happening right now), and 'B' stands for Background. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T1#BMP110_U2_T1_h5)

question: Why is a bedside handover usually better than just giving a report inside a closed office?

options.A: It shortens the total duration of the morning shift report
options.B: It allows direct visual checking of patients and equipment
options.C: It prevents relatives from asking questions about treatment
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for written case notes

explanation: Seeing is believing! Doing handover at the bedside lets incoming staff quickly check the patient with their own eyes and inspect drips or equipment. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T1#BMP110_U2_T1_h5)

question: What is the very first thing you should do if a piece of electrical equipment on the ward starts sparking?

options.A: Hide the device inside a drawer so no one else sees it
options.B: Disconnect the power source and label the equipment as faulty
options.C: Pour cold water over the electrical socket immediately
options.D: Continue using it carefully until the end of the shift

explanation: Safety first! Always switch off or unplug faulty equipment immediately and tag it out so nobody gets hurt. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T1#BMP110_U2_T1_h6)

question: You are setting up the emergency trolley on the labor ward. Which action shows great safety habits?

options.A: Checking drug expiry dates and ensuring all equipment is functional daily
options.B: Storing expired intravenous fluids at the bottom of the trolley
options.C: Locking the emergency trolley key inside the pharmacy store
options.D: Replacing emergency medications only when an inspector visits the ward

explanation: Emergency carts save lives. Doing quick daily checks guarantees that every drug and tool is ready and unexpired the exact moment an emergency strikes. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T1#BMP110_U2_T1_h6)
